item.title: Xi calls for new model of Sino-German cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
Xi calls for new model of Sino-German cooperation Countries urged to strengthen communication, coordination President Xi Jinping has called on China and Germany to build a new model of cooperation based on equality, mutual benefit and strategic stability, saying that the world's second- and third-largest economies should send a clear signal in favor of openness over closure and cooperation over confrontation amid growing global turbulence. When meeting with German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on Friday in Beijing, Xi urged the two countries to strengthen communication and coordination, citing their responsibilities for the development of relations between China and the European Union and stable growth of the global economy. China has always viewed the EU as a partner and has developed ties with it in a spirit of sincerity and goodwill, Xi said, adding that cooperation outweighs competition and consensus outweighs differences in China-EU relations. Xi noted that China-EU economic and trade ties are rooted in complementary strengths and mutual benefit. Mutual respect, understanding and accommodation pave the way to shared success, he said, emphasizing that seeking common ground amid differences and breaking new ground while upholding sound principles are key to advancing their development together. Problems arising from cooperation are part of the development of China-EU relations, Xi said. As long as China and the EU remain committed to their partnership and engage in dialogue on an equal footing, differences can be resolved without impeding the relations, he said. Xi expressed hope that the EU would work with China to advance an equal and orderly multipolar world and a universally beneficial and inclusive economic globalization. In terms of bilateral relationship, Xi emphasized that China's policy toward Germany remains consistent, stable and predictable. China attaches great importance to Germany's role as a major country, has long supported German unity and development, and welcomes a greater German role in European and international affairs, he said. Xi voiced hope that Germany would view cooperation with China and China's development with an open and positive mind, pursue a rational, pragmatic and friendly policy toward China, and uphold mutual respect and equal treatment. Complementary strengths Noting that Germany is known for advanced manufacturing and high-quality products, while China is pursuing modernization through high-quality development, Xi said their development strategies are well aligned, leaving broad scope for cooperation. China will continue to expand its high-level opening-up and improve its business environment, welcoming German and other foreign companies to deepen their presence in its vast market, Xi said. He also expressed the hope that Germany would provide Chinese companies with a fair, transparent and nondiscriminatory business environment. Xi identified artificial intelligence, green and low-carbon development, trade in services and the digital economy as areas where the two countries could work together and strengthen their future competitiveness. He called for more exchanges in culture, education and the arts, as well as easier travel between the two countries, in order to build closer ties between the two peoples ahead of the 55th anniversary of China-Germany diplomatic relations next year. Xi also briefed Steinmeier on the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China Central Committee. He said that sustained efforts to exercise full and rigorous Party self-governance would win broad public support, and expressed the CPC's willingness to exchange experience in governance with major political parties in Germany and other countries. Steinmeier said he had visited China eight times over the past 25 years and had seen a country transformed on each trip. Germany firmly adheres to the one-China policy and is confident about the future of bilateral relations, Steinmeier said. The two countries can handle trade differences through dialogue and consultation and pursue mutual benefit, setting an example for the world, he added. Germany is ready to work with China to defend the purposes and principles of the United Nations Charter and the authority of international law, support free trade and World Trade Organization rules, and oppose protectionism and trade wars, Steinmeier said. Germany has long been China's largest trading partner in the EU, while China was Germany's largest trading partner worldwide in 2025. The value of bilateral trade reached $211.11 billion last year, up 4.6 percent year-on-year. Speaking on Thursday at the German ambassador's residence in Beijing, Steinmeier cautioned against viewing China through simple binaries. "China is far too important for such simplifications — both economically and geopolitically," he said, calling for greater knowledge of China in Germany. Steinmeier's five-day state visit, which concludes on Saturday, follows German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's visit in February. Steinmeier began his trip in Anhui province, where he toured the former residence of Li Hongzhang, a leading statesman during the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911), who visited Germany in 1896. The German president visited Volkswagen Group China Technology Co in Anhui province, the group's largest research and development center outside Germany. He also visited Huangshan Mountain, a UNESCO World Cultural and Natural Heritage Site. Zhao Jizhou, an associate research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of European Studies, said the itinerary reflects Germany's interest in sustaining its historical, economic and cultural ties with China. Amid growing global uncertainty, Germany and Europe have a larger stake than ever in building stronger ties with China, which could bring greater stability to Europe and the wider world, Zhao said. Berlin's handling of trade frictions through dialogue with Beijing could help shape the course of China-EU relations, he added. zhaojia@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Iran: 'Carrot-and-stick' approach unworkable
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
Iran: 'Carrot-and-stick' approach unworkable Vance floats direct talks as US, Israel reportedly ready bombing campaign Tensions remain high across the Middle East, with Iran dismissing Washington's "carrot-and-stick" approach as unworkable, amid reports that the United States and Israel are preparing a potential weeklong bombing campaign against Iran after the upcoming midterm elections on Tuesday. Iran confirmed on Thursday it had received a letter from US Vice-President JD Vance but has yet to issue a response, Tasnim News Agency reported. The Wall Street Journal earlier said Vance sent the letter to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, in a bid to restart peace talks and avert another conflict. The paper quoted a source as saying that the letter was sent at the direction of US President Donald Trump, adding that "Vance is testing whether Tehran and Washington could find enough common ground to persuade Trump not to give a final order for a short, intense attack on Iran in the coming weeks". Iranian sources told Al Jazeera on Friday that the tone of Vance's letter is "much more respectful than previous ones" Tehran has received, which some see as "a positive sign". According to officials familiar with the matter, negotiations could kick off as early as next week in Qatar or Turkiye, potentially with no preconditions. US envoy Tom Barrack said late on Thursday that Washington and Tehran were "very close" to agreeing to a timeout to "bring temperatures down". Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, however, insisted Tehran's seven preconditions must first be met. "Iran's terms have been relayed clearly and repeatedly to mediators. The carrot-and-stick approach does not affect Iran," he posted on X. Trump said on Friday that he believed the conflict with Iran will end soon, but did not say how that would happen. "It's going to get wrapped up soon," Trump said in an interview with Kansas City radio station KCMO. "We need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon." Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Friday that three oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines while attempting to leave the Strait of Hormuz through an "unauthorized" southern route. It later said that it destroyed a US unmanned vessel in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. There was no immediate confirmation from the US military. Supply disruption fears Driven by supply disruption fears, oil prices climbed above $116 a barrel on Friday and are on track for a fourth consecutive monthly gain. According to Axios, US and Israeli officials are preparing for a potential seven-day military operation, although Trump has not made a final decision. Separately, The Associated Press reported that Washington has warned several Middle East countries to prepare for renewed military action and possible Iranian retaliation against energy facilities and other critical infrastructure. The Pentagon's latest estimate says the Iran conflict has cost US taxpayers $47.1 billion. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia has reportedly urged Washington not to rush into another military campaign and to allow regional mediators more time to secure an agreement. According to Axios, Saudi officials conveyed Tehran's concerns about a possible postelection bombing operation to the White House following recent diplomatic contacts. In a parallel development, final results from Israel's general election released on Friday showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc finished ahead of the opposition but fell short of an absolute majority in parliament. Netanyahu's coalition of right-wing and far-right parties secured 53 out of the Knesset's 120 seats. The opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot won 48 seats. The results from the Central Elections Committee also pointed to Arab-led parties as potential kingmakers, with the two winning a combined 19 seats. Netanyahu's party amplified unsubstantiated claims on Thursday that the Arab-led parties had "stolen" the election, possibly with foreign backing, as final tallies pointed to his bloc failing to secure a majority. Israeli media reported Likud members singled out Qatar, which quickly dismissed the allegations as "ridiculous and dangerous". Agencies and Xinhua contributed to this story.

item.title: Trilateral cooperation busts drug ring
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
Trilateral cooperation busts drug ring Chinese, Indonesian and Malaysian anti-drug authorities have jointly cracked a major transnational drug manufacturing and trafficking case, seizing about 1.2 metric tons of liquid methamphetamine and arresting 11 suspects in Indonesia, according to an announcement released by the Ministry of Public Security on Friday. On Oct 21, Indonesia's National Narcotics Agency dismantled a large-scale drug refining and production site in Banda Aceh, Indonesia, with strong support and assistance from the office of the China National Narcotics Control Commission and the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department of the Royal Malaysia Police. The operation followed a yearlong investigation by Chinese authorities that began in October 2025, when they uncovered leads pointing to a major criminal group involved in the international smuggling and trafficking of liquid drugs. Through extensive investigations, Chinese authorities gradually established that the group had repeatedly smuggled and trafficked liquid drugs into Indonesia. In September, the office of the China National Narcotics Control Commission shared information about the case with Indonesia's National Narcotics Agency. The two sides subsequently agreed to cooperate in a joint crackdown on the transnational criminal network. The Oct 21 operation marked a major achievement in cross-border anti-drug law enforcement cooperation and dealt a blow to drug-related crime in the region. yangzekun@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: China's Blue Bay initiative gets UN honor
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
China's Blue Bay initiative gets UN honor Nationwide marine restoration program lauded as a globally influential project China's Blue Bay Restoration Initiative was named a 2026 United Nations World Restoration Flagship on Thursday in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia, highlighting international recognition of China's achievements in marine ecological protection and restoration. The announcement was made at the "Restoration Day" event during the 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity, or COP17. Led by the Ministry of Natural Resources and the Ministry of Finance, the initiative is the second nationwide program from China to receive the honor, following the Shan-Shui Initiative, which was among the first global flagships in 2022. The achievement makes China the first country to have two nationwide actions recognized as World Restoration Flagships. The World Restoration Flagship, jointly established by the United Nations Environment Programme and the Food and Agriculture Organization, is a global recognition under the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, highlighting large-scale restoration projects that are exemplary, representative and globally influential. In this round, initiatives from Colombia, Ethiopia, Italy and the United States were also honored. At the awarding ceremony, Raimund Jehle, deputy regional representative for Europe and Central Asia at the Food and Agriculture Organization, underscored the importance of healthy coastal ecosystems for biodiversity, food security and people's livelihoods. "Healthy coastal ecosystems support fisheries, protect communities and strengthen resilience to climate change. Their restoration requires us to work across the boundaries between land and sea and across sectors and institutions," Jehle said. "China's Blue Bay Initiative demonstrates the value of this integrated approach, bringing together ecological restoration, coordinated governance and public investment," he added. Building on the experience of the Yundang Lake restoration in Xiamen, Fujian province, coastal regions across China have advanced integrated land-sea management and marine ecological restoration on a large scale. During the 13th (2016-20) and 14th Five-Year Plan periods (2021-25), China's central government allocated 36.63 billion yuan ($5.5 billion) to coastal provinces for the implementation of 194 major marine ecological restoration projects. This led to the restoration of more than 150,000 hectares of coastal wetlands, the management of Spartina alterniflora, an invasive cordgrass species, and the rehabilitation of more than 2,000 kilometers of coastline. Zhong Chongjun, deputy director-general of the ministry's department of territorial space ecological restoration, said the recognition demonstrates full acknowledgment from the international community of China's practical achievements in marine ecological protection and restoration. "The 194 major marine ecological restoration projects have effectively improved the quality and stability of key marine ecosystems, raised the level of biodiversity conservation, expanded quality coastal access for the public, enhanced coastal disaster prevention and mitigation capacity, and strengthened the marine ecological security barrier," Zhong said. "Thanks to sustained efforts, China's mangrove area has increased to 31,700 hectares, making the country one of the few in the world where mangrove coverage is continuously expanding," he added. Wang Lei, director-general of the department, described the selection as both "an honor and a responsibility". "We will take this as a new start, continuing to implement actions for blue bays, beautiful shorelines and harmonious islands," Wang said. He emphasized the focus on improving the quality and function of key marine ecosystems, such as mangroves, coral reefs, sea grass beds, and coastal salt marshes. The goal is to deliver more ecological restoration outcomes that enhance livelihoods, boost employment and income, and foster a new development paradigm of harmony between humanity and the sea. "We stand ready to deepen exchanges and cooperation with all countries, share our experience, build global consensus, jointly advance the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration and work hand in hand to safeguard our blue planet," Wang said.

item.title: Wukang Building charms visitors and residents
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
On a holiday morning, at the intersection of Middle Huaihai Road and Wukang Road in downtown Shanghai, a crowd of over a thousand people at any given moment converges on a single building. These visitors crane their phones upward, frame by frame, to shoot the 102-year-old wedge-shaped facade of Wukang Building, arguably the favorite architecture in Shanghai among visitors from home and abroad. Originally named Normandie Apartments and designed by Hungarian architect Laszlo Hudec in 1924, Shanghai's first veranda-style apartment block looks like a vessel with its "bow" pointing southwest. Renamed the Wukang Building in 1953 after China's liberation in 1949, the eightstory building was home to many film stars and cultural figures in the decades that followed. The building became viral among visitors after it completed a comprehensive renovation as part of the city's efforts to improve the quality of life for residents living in old buildings in 2019. Xuhui district data shows the wider Wukang-Anfu block draws 30,000 visitors on an average day since then, peaking near 100,000 on holidays, with Wukang Building quickly standing as a new landmark of Shanghai tourism. Clarisse Le Guernic, a French woman who has lived in Shanghai for 11 years and now serves as a "Shanghai international tourism ambassador", includes the building on nearly every downtown city walk route. "Foreign friends arriving here don't first look up at the building — they're stunned by the crowd," she said. "They ask: 'Why so many people? In Paris, we photograph the architecture. In China, people prefer photographing themselves with the architecture'." But for residents living in its 114 units, the place is more than a scenic spot to take photos. "For us, this is first of all a place to live," said Bai Zufang, Communist Party of China head of the Wukang residential community. Yet the building's most unusual chapter is not how it handles crowds, but how it managed the first problem its own residents raised. After the 2019 restoration — which took down exterior drying racks and awnings and aligned every air-conditioner unit — the question from residents was simple: "Where do we hang our laundry?" After discussions, the answer ended up on a rooftop platform that was originally the roof of the building's garage. The apartment block was built with a row of automobile garages at its base; the flat garage roof, level with the second floor, forms a wide open terrace that residents can step onto directly from the building. Since this rooftop platform sits directly above the garage, absolutely no drilling into the structure was allowed. To work around this, the heavy planting beds are kept securely in place using repurposed old tires filled with concrete. Rows of bamboo screens were also set up around the area — they gently block the view of residents hanging laundry to dry, while still letting fresh wind flow through the whole space. Carol Richman, a university lecturer from the US, has been inside the building once. "China is filled with wonderful historic buildings, yet this one carries a truly singular legacy all its own," she said. Contact the writers at heqi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Innovation in China driving global growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
Innovation in China driving global growth Positive sentiment among businesses reflected in foreign investment figures China's growing role as a source of global innovation is paying substantial dividends for international businesses, as the country remains committed to nurturing new quality productive forces and promoting greater market openness, a roundtable in Tianjin heard on Friday. The Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, a major economic engine in northern China, is at the forefront of the country's innovation drive, drawing on regional integration and international collaboration to spur growth, business executives and economists said. They made the remarks at the "CEO: Grow with China" roundtable, which was jointly organized by the Publicity Department of the Tianjin Municipal Committee of the Communist Party of China, China Daily and Tianjin Haihe Media Center. "Over the past few years, I have witnessed the ongoing transformation in China — from 'world's marketplace' into a 'global source of innovation'," said Claus Zieler, chief commercial and medical affairs officer at Astellas. The global drugmaker inaugurated its first innovation R&D center in China on Wednesday, completing a local value chain spanning research and development, manufacturing, sales and trade, he said. Astellas' growing presence in China is not an isolated phenomenon, but a reflection of the world's second-largest economy's sustained policy support for innovation. At the Central Economic Work Conference held in December, there were calls to develop an international technological innovation center in Beijing (Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region), with the region's stated aim being to become a world-class innovation engine by 2030. Speaking at the event, Xu Gang, executive deputy head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Tianjin Municipal Committee, said Tianjin is playing an active role in building the regional innovation center. Zhao Zhongxiu, a professor and former president of the University of International Business and Economics in Beijing, said the regional initiative is expected to forge closer ties between research and industry. "Competition in innovation increasingly extends to the capacity to bring scientific discoveries into productive use," Zhao said, adding that closer integration between scientific research and industrial innovation would create important opportunities during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) period. That connection between innovation and industry is also central to China's appeal among international businesses. "China's greatest opportunity for international business is no longer simply the size of its market, but its extraordinary capacity to transform innovation into industrial applications," said Gianni Di Giovanni, chairman of energy company Eni China. The ability to connect research, engineering, manufacturing and market demand gives China a fundamental competitive advantage, he said. According to Teo Eng Cheong, CEO of Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-City Investment and Development Co, companies can turn the country's wealth of scenarios and supply chain capabilities into competitive advantages, moving from "technology import" to "co-innovation" and contributing to global markets. This view was echoed by Gou Jianhui, chairman and CEO of Flender China, who sees the most compelling opportunity in "two-way collaboration: innovate in China, empower the world". The positive sentiment is reflected in China's foreign investment figures, with inflows into high-tech industries rising 33.8 percent year-on-year in the first nine months and accounting for 41.6 percent of the national total, according to the Ministry of Commerce. The confidence to invest also rests on an open and predictable business environment, which China is redoubling its efforts to provide as geopolitical risks and protectionism weigh on the global economy. Simon Lacey, founder of Market Access X, said China is moving in a genuinely positive direction in advancing high-standard opening-up. Gou from Flender China voiced similar confidence, saying the country's continued opening-up and improvements in its business environment send businesses a clear message of stability and long-term prospects. Tianjin, the roundtable's host city, is also pressing ahead with greater opening-up while working to improve its business environment. Andries De Bock, general manager of Leybold Equipment (Tianjin) Co, said a sound business environment is important for manufacturers, adding that his company's experience in the city has been positive. "Tianjin has become the largest open coastal city in northern China, with R&D spending reaching 3.47 percent of GDP, the fifth-highest level nationwide," said Ma Bo, president of Tianjin Haihe Media Center. "We welcome entrepreneurs from China and abroad to invest and innovate in Tianjin and pursue growth opportunities across the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region," said Xu from the Publicity Department of the CPC Tianjin Municipal Committee. Ren Qi, Li Jiaying, Tan Guoling and Wang Yubo contributed to this story.

item.title: China, Switzerland upgrade FTA
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-31
China, Switzerland upgrade FTA President Xi Jinping and President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin witnessed on Friday the signing of an upgraded free trade agreement, demonstrating the two countries' commitment to upholding openness and cooperation amid unilateralism and protectionism, as well as their distinctive role in promoting an open world economy. Parmelin started a three-day working visit to China on Friday. During their talks, Xi told the Swiss leader that Switzerland is an important partner of China in Europe and has consistently been at the forefront of cooperation between China and European countries. Switzerland was the first country on the continent of Europe to sign an FTA with China in 2013. In August this year, it became the first European country to conclude negotiations on upgrading the agreement. Xi said that bilateral free trade cooperation reflects the two countries' political courage and their sense of responsibility in upholding open cooperation. China is ready to work with Switzerland to uphold openness, strengthen cooperation and promote an inclusive and universally beneficial economic globalization, Xi said. The two sides should inject valuable confidence and greater certainty into China-Europe economic and trade cooperation and into global economic development, he added. Since the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1950, China and Switzerland have pursued cooperation based on mutual benefit and a pioneering spirit, achieving tangible results and demonstrating the principles of equality, innovation and win-win cooperation, Xi said. They have set an example for relations between countries of different sizes and with different social systems, Xi said. This year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Switzerland innovative strategic partnership, which is China's first strategic partnership with a foreign country centered on innovation. Xi called on the two sides to deepen innovation cooperation and foster collaboration in emerging industries, including the digital economy, green energy storage and artificial intelligence. Noting Switzerland's longstanding role in China-Europe economic and trade cooperation, Xi said he hopes that Switzerland will leverage its unique influence to play a positive role in promoting the sound, balanced and steady development of China-Europe trade. Parmelin said that Switzerland takes pride in being among the first Western countries to recognize the People's Republic of China — a decision that laid the foundation for a lasting and dynamic partnership between the two countries. He said the swift conclusion of negotiations on upgrading the FTA reflects the high level of mutual trust between the two countries and meets the expectations of businesses and other stakeholders on both sides. The upgraded agreement will inject fresh impetus into the development of Switzerland-China relations, Parmelin added. Data from the customs shows that China has remained Switzerland's third-largest trading partner for 12 consecutive years. The value of bilateral trade reached approximately $65.14 billion in the first half of 2026, registering substantial growth. In an article published on Monday by People's Daily, Qian Minjian, China's ambassador to Switzerland, said that once the upgraded China-Switzerland FTA takes effect, over 99 percent of goods exported by one country to the other will be duty-free, while market access will be further expanded in the areas of trade in services and investment. Feng Zhongping, a senior research fellow at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences' Institute of European Studies, said the upgrading of the China-Switzerland FTA comes at a critical time when economic and trade relations between China and the European Union are facing considerable uncertainty, with trade frictions continuing to weigh on bilateral ties. The upgraded FTA demonstrates the potential for China and European countries to achieve mutual benefit and shared development through cooperation, he added. jihaisheng@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: German president plays ping-pong at PKU
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-30
German president plays ping-pong at Peking University Share - WeChat
On Oct 29, German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier visited Peking University and played friendly table tennis matches with students and faculty at the Khoo Teck Puat Gymnasium. The gymnasium hosted the table tennis event of the Beijing 2008 Olympic Games. Teaming up with Liu Wei, a professor in the university's Physical Education Department and a world table tennis champion, Steinmeier faced Peking University President Gao Song and German table tennis legend Timo Boll in an exhilarating match.

item.title: Former Kyrgyz PM hails CPC's self-governance practices
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
Former Kyrgyz PM hails CPC's self-governance practices Share - WeChat
Djoomart Otorbaev, former prime minister of Kyrgyzstan, said in a recent interview that the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China Central Committee is of great significance. He praised the CPC's continued efforts to strengthen Party discipline, pursue self-reform and adapt to changing circumstances and emerging challenges. Otorbaev said the CPC's approach to self-governance has played a key role in China's development and offers a valuable example for countries across the Global South.
